newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares firm, wary of U.S. CPI.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares firm, wary of U.S. CPI.

text.p: Leading Russian shares firmed in early trading on Tuesday and dealers said they expected prices to rise further for most of the day subject to a March inflation report due out in the U.S. later in the day.

"I expect the market to be slightly up until 5 o'clock and then we'll see what happens. If the CPI (Consumer Price Index) is up it will be one less headache," said Bobby Meshoyrer, director of sales and trading at Aton.
The Russian Trading System 23-share index opened slightly down at 285.50 after Monday's 286.07 close.
Power utility and market benchmark UES rose to $0.2075 at 0815 GMT after closing lower at $0.2009 on Monday and energy company Mosenergo nosed up to $1.194 from $1.170 previously.
"We're seeing a bit of a pickup in Mosenergo and RAO UES and UES represents the whole market right now -- if people want to see how the market is doing they look at UES," said Meshoyrer.
Traders said the market was looking livelier after a slow day on Monday and said money was starting to trickle back into the market after sales of the last few weeks.

"I think that money that was taken out of the market a few weeks ago is going back in at lower levels. I think the market will close with a plus today," said Alexander Fonarkov, a trader at Regent European Securities.
But he said developments on Wall Street, including a widely-expected interest rate hike in mid-May, would continue to affect the emerging Russian market.
Until then, we'll have a very shaky situation with the market in the range of five percent," Fonarkov said.
But other dealers were less worried.
"Based on the last couple of months inflation is better than expected and so hopefully everything will be fine and people will be looking at Russia," said Meshoyrer.
